subject: Note-decay E: subsumption (FadeMem) — merge/refine when a new note is more specific/general than an existing one
description:
Borrow FadeMem's Subsumptive/Subsumed classes. Forks off orch/feature/note-decay.

SCOPE: Today the dup-cluster pass (lib/judge.js dupClusters) handles SAME-fact consolidation (supersede). Extend it to detect DIRECTIONAL subsumption — a new note strictly MORE SPECIFIC or MORE GENERAL than an existing current note — and MERGE/REFINE (produce a consolidated note that supersedes both, or refine the keeper) rather than treating them as independent duplicates. Reuse the soft-retire/supersede primitive (note_superseded); keep full history. Tests. Commit onto orch/attempt/<key> before complete_task.

summary: Implemented FadeMem subsumption (Note-decay E). Added `cosineSim`, `findSubsumedNotes`, and `SUBSUMPTION_THRESHOLD=0.92` to `lib/judge.js`. Hooked into the `POST /overlay/note` (record_decision) handler in `routes/overlay.js`: after ingestNode, calls findSubsumedNotes, stamps `validTo`/`supersededBy` on each subsumed older note node, and appends a `note_superseded` graphStore event — guarded by `if (b.vec)` and wrapped best-effort. Added 25 plain-Node tests in `test/note-decay-subsumption.test.js` covering all gate conditions. All 25 new tests and all pre-existing tests pass.
